title: Knowledge check: Testing User Interactions

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Testing User Interactions”?
options: Make end-to-end tests the only test level.
Test observable behavior with deterministic setup, realistic interaction, and both a normal case and a relevant failure or boundary case.
Test only private implementation details and ignore user-visible behavior.
Rely on one screenshot as proof of every application state.
questions.answer_key: Test observable behavior with deterministic setup, realistic interaction, and both a normal case and a relevant failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Testing User Interactions directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Triggering DOM events”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Choose tests around observable behavior and cover normal plus edge or failure cases.
A screenshot alone proves all component states are correct.
Mock every function even when a real unit test is clearer.
End-to-end tests should be the only test type.
questions.answer_key: Choose tests around observable behavior and cover normal plus edge or failure cases.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Triggering DOM events”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Testing User Interactions” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
